language.label: Language
language.help: The language the game's words are written in. Others come as they are translated.

textSpeed.label: Text speed
textSpeed.help: How fast what people say is written out. The A button always finishes a line at once.

help.High: Sharpest picture: the 3D scenes render at 4K (3840 × 2160) with soft shadows and ambient occlusion.
help.Medium: 3D scenes render at 2880 × 1620 with anti-aliasing; keeps soft shadows and ambient occlusion.
help.Low: Fastest: 3D scenes render at 1920 × 1080 with simple shadows, no ambient occlusion or depth of field.

windowSize.label: Window size
windowSize.help: Size of the game window when it isn't full screen.

vsync.label: V-Sync
vsync.help: Matches the display's refresh rate to avoid tearing.

help.fixed: The world stays at this time of day.
help.clock: Follows your computer's clock, like the original: morning from 4, day from 10, twilight from 17, night from 20.

sound.label: Sound
sound.help: Music and sound effects (also the M key).

music.label: Music
music.help: How loud the music and the fanfares play.

soundEffects.label: Sound effects
soundEffects.help: How loud the sound effects play: menus, doors, footsteps, the moves in battle.

cries.label: Cries
cries.help: How loud the Pokémon's cries play.

ambience.label: Ambience
ambience.help: How loud the field's background sounds play: rain, wind, waterfalls, the sea, caves.

help.Stereo: Full sound, for speakers or headphones.
help.Handheld: Sounds as the handheld's own small speakers would: no deep bass, a narrow stereo and ten-bit sound.
help.Mono: Everything in one channel, the same in both ears: for a single speaker, or one ear.

rules.other: Rules follows the rules the game was begun under.

moveHints.label: Move hints
moveHints.help: In battle, a move's card says whether it is super effective, not very effective or has no effect on a Pokémon you have seen before.
moveHints.modern: Rules: this game is played by the modern rules, so it shows them.
moveHints.platinum: Rules: this game is played by Platinum's rules, so it goes without.

trainerLines.label: Trainers speak
trainerLines.help: In battle, Gym Leaders, your rival and other bosses say a line when their last Pokémon comes out, when their first one falls and when their last one is in the red.
trainerLines.modern: Rules: this game is played by the modern rules, so it has them speak.
trainerLines.platinum: Rules: this game is played by Platinum's rules, so it keeps them quiet, as Platinum did.

help.on: While another window is in front, the game waits where it is and its sound drops; it goes on when you come back to it.
help.off: The game runs on, sound and all, while another window is in front.

help.capped: The most frames the game draws a second. V-Sync, when it is on, still holds it to the display's refresh rate.
help.none: The game draws as many frames a second as it can. V-Sync, when it is on, still holds it to the display's refresh rate.

help.Off: Every scene of the story plays through, as in Platinum.
help.Seen: Hold the menu button for a second to skip a scene of the story you have already seen to its end, in this game or another on this computer. Questions and battles are never skipped.
help.Any: Hold the menu button for a second to skip any scene of the story, seen or not. Questions and battles are never skipped.

help.on: Moves and the battle's other animations play, as in Platinum.
help.off: No moves or other animations play in battle: the lines and the HP bars alone, for quicker battles.

help.Shift: When a trainer's Pokémon faints, you are told which comes out next and asked whether to switch first, as in Platinum.
help.Set: When a trainer's Pokémon faints, the next one comes straight out and you are not asked to switch.

help.label: Help
help.help: The type chart, the controls and a few notes for the road.

recovered.heading: Slot {slot}'s last save was damaged
recovered.body: It couldn't be read, perhaps because the game closed while it was being written. The save made before it has been loaded instead.

damaged.heading: Slot {slot} can't be read
damaged.body: Its save and the one kept before it are both damaged, so that game can't be continued. DELETE A SAVE frees the slot for another.

noFreeSlot.heading: Every slot holds a save
noFreeSlot.body: A new game needs a slot of its own, and all three are taken. DELETE A SAVE, on this menu, frees one of them.

couldNotDelete.heading: Slot {slot} couldn't be deleted
couldNotDelete.body: Its files are still there: something else may be using them. Nothing was changed; try again once it is closed.

oldSaveNoRoom.heading: An older save was left where it is
oldSaveNoRoom.body: {file} is from before the game had slots, and all three slots hold a save. Once one is deleted, the next start gives it that slot.

oldSaveFailed.heading: An older save couldn't be moved
oldSaveFailed.body: {file} is from before the game had slots and couldn't be given one. It is where it was, untouched; the next start tries again.

crash.heading: The game stopped unexpectedly
crash.noSave: No game had been saved yet.
crash.reportKept: A report was written to {report}, and the game as it stood was kept beside your save as {file}.

blurb.one: It will be saved in slot {slot}. The save you have is kept as it is.
blurb.other: It will be saved in slot {slot}. The saves you have are kept as they are.

delete.heading: Delete slot {slot}?
delete.unreadable: This save can't be read, nor can the one before it. Deleting it frees the slot.
delete.blurb: {name}, {time} played. The save and its backup are deleted for good.
delete.blurbIn: {name} in {place}, {time} played. The save and its backup are deleted for good.

rules.heading: Which rules?
rules.platinumBlurb: Battles play exactly as they do in Platinum, which the story is balanced for. This can't be changed later.
rules.modernBlurb: Battles use the newest games' numbers for critical hits, burns, paralysis and moves. This can't be changed later.

quit.heading: Quit the game?
quit.body: Anything since your last save will be lost unless you save first.

close.heading: Close the game?
close.cantSave: The game can't be saved right now: anything since your last save will be lost.

help.title: HELP

about.title: Getting about
about.text: Hold the run button once you have the Running Shoes. Talk to people and read signs with the confirm button: many have something to give or to say about the road ahead.

battle.title: In battle
battle.text: A move of a type the foe is weak to does twice the damage, and one its two types are both weak to four times. The TYPES page has every matchup; the move hints in the options can say it on the move's card.

poketch.title: The Pokétch
poketch.text: Once you have it, put it on the screen and change its app with their buttons, and take it in hand to touch it: the arrows move a cursor over its buttons.

saving.title: Saving
saving.text: Save from the menu whenever you like. A Pokémon Center heals your team for nothing, and the last one you visited is where you wake up after losing a battle.

super.headline: Super effective
super.line: A {attack} move against a {defend} Pokémon does twice the damage.

half.headline: Not very effective
half.line: A {attack} move against a {defend} Pokémon does half the damage.

none.headline: No effect
none.line: A {attack} move does nothing at all to a {defend} Pokémon.

plain.headline: A plain matchup
plain.line: A {attack} move against a {defend} Pokémon does its usual damage.

help.twoTypes: Against two types, both count: ×2 and ×2 make four times, ×2 and ×½ cancel out.

outfits.ownDescription: What you set out in. You can always change back into it.
outfits.buyNote: Yours for good, to wear at home too.
outfits.bought: You bought the {garment} and put it on!

ceremony.welcome: WELCOME TO THE HALL OF FAME

digging.title: THE WALL

pick.name: PICK
pick.note: One layer round the blow. The wall loses a little.

hammer.name: HAMMER
hammer.note: Two layers, and the corners. The wall loses more.

ringsHollow.one: The wall rings hollow in one place!
ringsHollow.other: The wall rings hollow in {n} places!

digging.lesson: Chip the wall away with the pick or the hammer. The hammer takes more off at a blow, and brings the wall down the sooner!
digging.allDug: Every last thing is out of the wall!
digging.noRoom: There's no room for it in the bag. It was left behind.

belowGround.noSpheresYet: None yet. Dig some out of a wall.
belowGround.sphereNote: Buried in the floor of a tunnel, a Sphere grows a little every day. The hikers take them in trade.
belowGround.treasureNote: Dug out of a wall. Put in the bag, it is an item like any other above ground.

goUp.name: GO UP
goUp.note: Back to the surface, where you went down.

belowGround.decorateNote: Put goods out of the PC about the base, put them away again, or move them.

trap.drill: Used facing a wall of the tunnels, it opens a secret base there. One drill, one base: a second base moves the first.
trap.slide: Whoever steps on it is sent sliding the way its arrow points, until something stops them.
trap.hole: Whoever steps on it falls in, and has to wriggle this way and that to climb out.
trap.steering: Whoever steps on it finds their steps going the wrong way for a while.
trap.smoke: Whoever steps on it is wrapped in smoke until they have wiped it away.
trap.rock: A boulder drops in front of whoever steps on it, and has to be broken up.
trap.bubbles: Whoever steps on it is buried in bubbles until every one is burst.
trap.alert: It calls out when someone steps on it. Nothing more.
trap.leaves: Whoever steps on it is covered in leaves until they are blown away.
trap.fire: A flame springs up before whoever steps on it, and has to be blown out.

good.trap: {size} of a secret base, and goes off like a trap under whoever steps on it.

hiker.noSpheres: No Spheres on you? Come back when you've dug some up.

hiker.fairSwap: A fair swap! You got a {sphere} of size {size}.
hiker.nowhere: Hold on, you've nowhere to put it!
hiker.wrongSphere: No, no. It's another colour of Sphere I'm after.
hiker.tooSmall: Too small, that one. I want a bigger Sphere for it.

counter.foeText: For Castle Points the valet tells which Pokémon come next, moves their levels up or down by five, and tells their stats and moves. A Pokémon raised five levels is worth more Castle Points when it is beaten.
